text: The second day of the Satipatthana course is over. This evening let us go through this discourse and understand in relation to the actual practice that we are doing. The name of the discourse is Mahasatipatthana Sutthana, Sutthana means discourse. It is said Mahasatipatthana, the word maha means great, big. That means there is something smaller than this and yes there is another discourse given by Buddha on Satipatthana which is smaller than this discourse. This discourse is maha, bigger because it gives, it deals with some more subjects in detail therefore it is called Mahasatipatthana. Sati is awareness, a very important faculty of dhamma as we discussed yesterday. Sati is one of our indriyas, a faculty which one has to master to develop in dhamma. Sati is one of the bala, the forces, the strength which one must develop to master dhamma. Sati is one of the factors of enlightenment which one has to develop to get fully enlightened. Sati is also one of the eight full noble paths, samma, sati. Sati plays a very important role in the practice of dhamma. The literal meaning of the word sati is and very commonly used nowadays in other languages of India, present languages of India as smriti which means memory, remembrance. But when you practice vipashyana there is no memory involved, you are not remembering something of the past. Here what you have to remember is, remember your object of meditation. That means the reality within the framework of the body, the reality pertaining to mind and matter. You should always remember that your mind does not wander away from this reality. That is in that sense you can say remembrance. But in a better way of understanding let us say sati means awareness and this is what it is. You are aware. You can't be aware of the past, you can't be aware of the future. You can be aware of the present. The reality of this moment as it is, this is sati, pathana. One gets established. The word pa says extensively, you get established extensively. What extensively? That means it is not mere awareness, along with that awareness there is element of panya, element of wisdom. You are not merely aware of the truth pertaining to mind and matter, you are also aware of the nature of this truth pertaining to mind and matter, how it keeps on arising, passing away, arising, passing away, how it is a source of misery, how it is no I, no mind, how it is substance-less. All that has not to be understood merely at the intellectual level with direct experience. And therefore pathana, panya, the bhavanamaya panya is there, with your own direct experience you develop your awareness with the wisdom which makes you understand the reality in its true nature, not just as it appears to be, not just as it seems to be, but in its true nature and that is why it is maha sati pathana sutta. When the discourse starts, evam me sutam, this is what was heard by me, this was heard by me. These are not the words of buddha, somebody else says, this was heard by me. These are the words of someone else, there is a history behind it and a very important history which a vipassana meditator should know. At the ripened age of 80 years when buddha passed away, most of his students who were present at that time and who had reached the final goal of arhanthood, fully liberated, they understood the law of nature, everyone who takes birth has to pass away. Whether one is buddha or an ordinary person makes no difference. When time ripens, one has to pass away. For those who were not developed in dhamma, they felt very sorry, very sad, some of them even started crying. There was one person who felt very happy. An old monk, in age old, not in wisdom, he felt very happy, oh good, this old man has passed away. All the time we were under his clutches, do this, don't do this, do this, don't do this, now we are free to do whatever we like. One of his teachings, attahi attanonathu, you are your own master, now I can be my own master, wonderful. That shows that such elements had entered in the sangha who were not interested in dhamma. They just took robes because they found by entering the sangha, becoming a monk in the name of buddha, will give them some status in the society. They can live a comfortable life, people will give more arms to them than they would have received otherwise, and they will get more respect, they were not interested in dhamma. Now this person, I feel extremely grateful to this person, thankful to this person, why? Because when he announced that wonderful buddha has passed away, one of the chief disciples of buddha, when he heard this, he thought even today if there are such people, what is going to happen in the future, later on such elements will become predominant, and they will just distort the teaching of buddha in their own way, and actually this happened also after some time. How to save it? The words of buddha, the teachings of buddha, he became enlightened at the age of 35, and he passed away at the age of 80, for 45 years, day and night, hardly two or three hours he will lie down for sleep, which is not sleep, awareness and equanimity, awareness and wisdom, to give rest to the body, rest of the time he was just teaching dhamma. He taught, he gave 82,000 sermons. Over 2,000 sermons were given by leading disciples of buddha, who were urhans. So in all 84,000 sermons. Now this elderly disciple, by the name of Mahakassapa, he decides that all the teaching of buddha must be compiled together, and we should try to preserve it for the coming generations, so that people do not change it. Quite possible later on, persons like this fellow will put their own words in the mouth of buddha and they will say, buddha said so, they will take freedom from certain disciplines which are very essential for the progress of dhamma, and they will say, buddha gave this permission, and things like that, which after a few centuries it did happen. We must preserve the actual words of buddha, while there are people who are direct disciples of buddha, who are eyewitness to buddha's teaching, who heard buddha's teaching. So he decided to call a meeting of 500 urhans, fully liberated persons, elderly persons, elderly monks, let us sit together and recite all the teachings of buddha, compile them, and announce it as authenticated. This is just immediately after the death of buddha. If this is compiled after 100 years or 200 years, people may accept, may not accept, it should be done now. So this Mahakasapa, a very wise person, he made this decision, he gathered 500 elderly urhans, well even a few handful could do that, but just to impress the people of that time and people of future, 500 of them joined together, and they read out every word, they recited every word of buddha, and then gave it a seal of authenticity. When he selected 500, somebody said no, this congregation, this gathering will not be a perfect gathering unless we have ananda as one of the members. So have only 499, let ananda be a member to make it 500. Now who is this ananda? Buddha was cousin brother of buddha, Gautama the buddha, was born on the same day as Gautama the buddha was born. He was with him in the childhood, he was with him during the youth, and when buddha renounced the householder's life, went out and became enlightened, then he was one amongst many family members who also renounced their householder's life and joined him, and since then he was with him all the time. When buddha started teaching, the number of followers started spreading, the work started spreading, naturally he wanted some assistant, a number of assistants came near him to help him, to serve him, but quite a few of them came with some motives, the motive was, here he is a fully enlightened person, he is against these miracles, he has the power of miracles, no doubt, but he doesn't want his followers to show miracles. If I am very close to him, I will be fortunate to see some of the miracles being performed by him, such motive was there with some of these attendants, personal attendants. Buddha had refused to answer certain questions, philosophical questions, he said they are useless, meaningless, don't waste your time on them. Now some attendants thought that he doesn't want to say anything on this subject in public, but perhaps if I am very close, then he may explain, I better be very close, I better serve. Such people could not stay with him longer, sooner or later they have to leave. People keep on changing and as he grew in age, he became 55 years old, getting old, so people thought that there must be a stable personal assistant with him, he also accepted yes some responsible stable personal assistant, a private secretary is necessary. Many of the elderly monks were very eager to take that post, to serve him so closely, but Buddha had a liking towards Ananda, and Ananda is mum, he doesn't say a word, people know that if Ananda says yes, Buddha will accept him, Ananda does not say yes, when they persuaded him he said I have got my terms, if Buddha accepts my terms, then I will be his personal assistant, somebody putting terms before Buddha to be a personal assistant, what are your terms? He put up some seven or eight terms, and out of that one was very healthy terms, very wholesome terms. One of that was that whenever you give any discourse anywhere, if I am present, perfectly alright, if by any reason I am not present and you give a discourse, then when you come back you must repeat that discourse to me. Buddha accepted all his conditions, including this, so from the age of 55 to the age of 80, 25 years, every discourse that Buddha gave was heard by this person, Ananda, even the discourses before that also were heard by him, but these 25 years he was like a shadow with Buddha, every discourse was heard by him, and here was a wonderful person, he had such a wonderful faculty, from some of his good parmes of the past, and also due to his practice of this life, he had developed the faculty of memory, he hears something once, enough, it is like tape recorded, what you are doing here, it is like computerized, anytime you ask anything, he will just repeat word to word, this was his wonderful faculty. So people said if Ananda is not there, something is missing, he should be there, but he can't be there, because this is a gathering of Arhans, and he is not an Arhan. Understand Ananda served Buddha for 25 years, so close to him, Ananda was his cousin brother, so close to him, Ananda was his great devotee, so close to him, and yet he could not become Arhan, he was only Sotapanna, the first stage of liberation, when one experiences the liberation stage, the stage beyond mind and matter for the first time, very important stage, but still it is the first stage of liberation, after that you have got higher stage, you have got higher stage than that, and then you have the highest stage of Arhan, and here he is having reached only the first stage, this again for us to understand that Buddha cannot liberate anybody, each individual has to work out one's own salvation, he had no time, he was just serving Buddha all the time, he could not progress, although he knew Dhamma perfectly well, not one, not two, thousands of persons whom he taught became Arhans, and he himself was not Arhan, and in this gathering, how can a known Arhan be there, so Mahakasrapa goes to him and tells him, well look, well look, Vandivalananda, you were very busy serving Buddha, now Buddha is no more, you know the technique so well, because your own disciples have reached the stage of Arhanthood, now you have got so much time, why not work, become Arhan, so that you can come in our gathering, join our gathering, this is the aim that we have of this gathering, and you will be very great asset to it, Ananda was very glad, wonderful, yes, I didn't have much time before, now I have got time, nothing else, all time is there at my disposal, wait for few days, I will practice, I will become Arhanth and join you, and he started working, started working very vigorously, I must become an Arhanth, I must become an Arhanth, when he was teaching others, he used to say, don't develop ego, this ego is dangerous for you, it will be an obstacle, and when he practices himself, this ego becomes important, I must become Arhanth, I must become Arhanth, many a time the teacher forgets what he teaches others, when he practices himself, he forgets his own teaching and this is what happened, he didn't move an inch, now tomorrow they have to start this conference, and Mahakasrappa comes to Ananda and tells him, look we have waited so long, we can't be waiting, there are 499 persons waiting for the conference to start by tomorrow morning, you are Arhanth or no Arhanth, if you are no Arhanth, I take somebody else, I will start my work, if you are Arhanth, you are welcome, yes, yes, yes, one night more, I will try this one night more, and again try, try, I must become Arhanth, this is the only night for me, I must become Arhanth, the first part of the night, the middle part of the night, the last part of the night, light passes away, the sun is rising, he is so exhausted, he doesn't cry, at least this good quality, he is not successful, and that much he knows that one should not cry when one is not successful, he accept the fact, well I accept the fact, I am not an Arhanth, now let me take rest, let me take rest, I am not an Arhanth, I am just a Sotapanna, a Sotapanna, he was with the reality of this moment as it is, when he was aiming for something to become Arhanth, his mind was always in the future, not in the present, and now I am not an Arhanth, he accept this reality, I am just a Sotapanna, I am taking rest, I am taking rest, and observing the sensations inside, arising, passing, arising, passing, this is the way of taking rest, for good meditators, I am taking rest, and before his head could reach the pillow, he was an Arhanth, when you, how much effort, if you make over-exertion, then you lose the balance of your mind, middle path, neither there must be one extreme of laxity that you don't do anything, nor your effort must be so extreme that you lose the balance of your mind, and Ananda becomes Arhanth, and Ananda becomes Arhanth, and he joins the conference. Now questions are asked to Ananda, what did Buddha say? All the teachings of Buddha were compiled, and three divisions were made, that is why they are called Ti Pitika, Ti means three, Pitika means baskets, baskets in those days, the books were kept in baskets, there is three groups of the teaching of Buddha, the one is Sutta Pitaka, where is long or short discourses to the public were accumulated, compiled, then Vinaya Pitaka, his discourses specially to the monks, the nuns, about their discipline, about their Seela, for householders five Seela, good enough, but for a monk, for a nun, over 200 Seelas, and this is what this old man resented, oh so much restriction on us, all those instructions to the monks, to the nuns, they were given by the monks, they were compiled in Vinaya Pitaka, and then the third called Abhidhamma, higher Dhamma, Dhamma, law of nature, the truth, deeper truth, which it is not easy to understand by ordinary person, one has to meditate very deeply to understand it, this is an analytical study of the entire mind-matter phenomenon, the entire field, in such detail it is explained in Abhidhamma, starting from the apparent truth to the ultimate truth, all the details of the reality pertaining to the matter, all the details of the reality pertaining to the mind, all the details pertaining to the reality, reality pertaining to the mental factors, the mental concomitants, the mental contents, the matter in the language of those days was called Rupa, the mind was called Chitta, and the mental contents, Chetashika, fully explained how they interact, how one starts influencing the other, how the matter stimulates the arising of the mind, how the mind stimulates the arising of the matter, how the mind stimulates the arising of the mind, how the matter stimulates the arising of the matter, all these interconnections and the currents and cross currents going on deep inside are fully explained, they cannot be understood just by reading Abhidhamma, only by the practice of Vipashyana, at a very deep stage such things become clear, that is the third Pethaka, Abhidhamma Pethaka, all these three, so far as Sutta Pethaka, and Abhidhamma Pethaka were concerned, Ananda was asked questions about that, so far as Vinaya Pethaka was concerned, another Arhant by the name of Upali, he was perfect in the discipline of monks and nuns, he was asked questions, now this comes in the Sutta Pethaka, and Ananda says, this is what I heard, Evam Me Sutam, in many of these Suttas, we find the Sutta start with these words, Evam Me Sutam, this is what I heard, he heard directly from the Mahavata Buddha, this is what I heard, and then he is good enough to give a description of the situation, the situation in which this discourse was given, when it was given, to whom it was given, in what circumstances it was given, and how it was given, all that sort of preamble he gives there, and then the actual Sutta starts, so now that explanation, as to where it was given, and he says, Ekam Samayam Bhagava, at one time, Bhagava means the enlightened one, the Buddha, Ekam Samayam Bhagava, Kurusu Viharati, Viharati was living, the word Viharati is not used for ordinary lay people in the language of India, Viharati is used for very enlightened persons, and even those who are on the path of enlightenment, like the monks, the nuns, or even lay people who are practicing Dhamma, this word is used, Viharati, so Buddha was at that time, he was living in the world of the enlightened, and in Dhamma, this word is used, Viharati, so Buddha was at that time living, staying in Kuru, Kuru was one of the sixteen states of northern India of those days, it is somewhere near today's Delhi, near Punjab, adjacent to Rajasthan, which is now called Haryana, a state which is now called Haryana, was called Kuru in those days, and it was here that this discourse was given, Ekam Samayam Bhagava, Kurusu Viharati, Viharati, Viharati, Viharati, that this discourse was given, Ekam Samayam Bhagava, Kurusu Viharati, and in Kuru, in this state also where, Kammas Dhammanam Kurunam Nigamu, a small district of this state by the name of Kammas Dhamma, this was the name of this place where this discourse was given, this discourse was given, Tattrakho Bhagava Bhikkhu Aamante Shri Bhikkha Bhooti, Buddha called those who were present, called them as O Bhikkhus, and Bhadan Te Bhikkhu Bhagavato Pachasosum, and those Bhikkhus, they replied back, Bhadan Te, yes Vendables Sir. Now two things to understand, this important sermon was given in Kuru, Buddha had very high words to say about the people of Kuru, and not only Buddha, later on also, in other traditions also, Kuru is taken as a place where people, most of the people live the life of Buddha, and Kuru is taken as a place where people, most of the people live the life of Buddha, and Kuru is taken as a place where people live the life of Buddha, and Kuru is taken as a place where people live the life of Buddha, and Kuru is taken as the field of Dhamma, the field of Kuru, it talks of Kuru, which is the field of Dhamma, why it is taken with such high regard, Buddha explains in one of his other discourses, long ago, when Buddha was not Buddha, in his previous lives, he had the seed of Buddhahood, he was developing his parmes to become Buddha, the ten parmes, and from life to life, he was living a good life to develop his own parme, in one of the lives, he was king of Kuru, now the people of Kuru, right from the king, to the smallest person, they all observe Sheela, they all observe Sheela, those were the days, when what you call Pancha Sheela now, the five precepts, what you call Sheela Dhamma, the Dhamma of Sheela, morality, in the language of those days of India, it was called Kuru Dhamma, the Dhamma of Kuru, that means the people of Kuru have got this nature, this is their nature, they live the life of morality, everyone lives the life of morality, quite peculiar, at that time, the would-be Buddha, the Bodhisatta, was the ruler of this country, Kuru, and it so happened, that one of the states of India of those days, which is today called Orissa, in those days it was called Kalinga, there was famine, drought, year after year, year after year, people became very miserable, and there was a belief, that these famines come, when people don't live the life of morality, and people don't live the life of morality, when the ruler is not living the life of morality, so the elders of this state, this kingdom, went to the king, to the ruler, and said, sir, there is something wrong, look year after year, famine is there, something should be done, our people should live the life of morality, and this cannot happen unless you start living the life of morality, so take five precepts, and let all the public, all the people of the state take five precepts and observe, and to take five precepts, it is important that it is taken from somebody, who is perfect in five precepts, so from whom you should take five precepts, from whom we should take five precepts, we better approach the ruler of Kuru, he is a perfect person, and all his people, all his subjects, they are living the life of morality, the five precepts are there, so two ambassadors were sent to the kingdom of Kuru, two Brahmin ambassadors, they reached there, and told the whole story to the ruler, we are in difficulty, please give us these five precepts, you write it on a slate, and we will take that, and on your behalf, we will read out to the teacher, and then we will read out to all the people, and we will start practicing, and we will be out of misery, the king refuses, he says, yes I have been living a perfect life of Seela, but there is one slight mistake which I committed, one slight mistake, so I am not perfect, and he asked his ambassadors, you better go to him, he asked them to go to his mother, elderly mother, she is perfect, they go to the mother, mother says no, no, no, this one little mistake I did in my life, you better go to the queen, the chief queen, and they go to the chief queen, and she says no, no, no, no, one little mistake I have done, then go to the younger brother of the king, and then go to the prime minister of the state, then go to this revenue minister of the state, then you go to the chief priest of the state, then you go to this chief officer of the state, revenue officer of the state, then you go to this chief trader of the state, business man of the state, and like this they went And like this they went on going to different, different, everyone says it was slight, slight mistake in my life, slight mistake in my life. And coming down, down, down, the charioteer, go to the charioteer. They went to the charioteer, he says no, some mistake. Then go to the watchman who takes care of the gate. Some mistake. Like this from the king down, everybody are so very much careful about their precepts. And the mistakes that they have said, we won't go in all those details, it will take time, are so flimsy. Like for example, the king he says, I made a mistake, what mistake? He says once I was showing my art of archery, I am wonderful in using the bow and the arrow and I was just showing this to my people, my subject. And one arrow which I threw, it went and fall in the pond nearby. And when it fell in the pond, it went inside and didn't come up. It didn't come up. That shows it must have pierced some fish there and with the weight of the dead fish it remained, it didn't come up. Well, who knows, whether really it pierced a fish or it might have gone in the depth of the mud at the bottom and would not have come up or some other obstacle. But he doubts, perhaps, perhaps by my action, one fish would have been killed, unlike that. People are so careful about their shield. Now this is a country where from the past tradition people are careful about their morality. So this discourse does not talk about morality, morality base is there, he is talking to the people of that country. Base of morality is essential, but base is base. The gap between one Buddha and the another Buddha, this is what happens. When a Buddha arises, an enlightened person arises, he gives complete dhamma, the totality of it, pure dhamma, there is nothing which can be taken out of it, there is no trace of impurity that has to be taken out, there is nothing wanting which has to be added, keval paripunam, keval parishuddham, the dhamma that is taught by an enlightened person is so complete and so pure. But as time passes, as time passes, this complete pure dhamma becomes incomplete, incomplete. Certain important portions get disappearing, they disappear, they disappear. The most difficult ones, they start disappearing earlier, the panya starts disappearing, vipashana starts disappearing. The panya which remains is panya, only intellectual panya, people keep on talking about panya, keep on talking about wisdom, but the practice, the bhavana maya panya gets lost. The samadhi, the purer part of samadhi goes away, the concentration, concentration with some verbalisation or visualisation or imagination, that will remain. But the samadhi which develops with the awareness of the reality, that passes away. And what remains is sila. And now that sila becomes so important to people, yes, it is important, but the other factors, the other steps of dhamma are lost, then more importance is given to sila. People start going to extreme, they start stretching the sila, one sila or the other to such an extent that the mind becomes unbalanced. They can't practice proper samadhi, they can't practice proper panya. We find same thing happening in today's India also, there are sections of the society where they stretch one sila or the other to such an extent, to such an extent that they lose the balance of their mind. They can't practice proper samadhi, they can't practice proper panya. This is what Buddha kept on condemning. He said, sila vata paramasya, paramasya is attachment, attachment to such a great extent that by observing this particular sila, I am going to get liberation, I will be liberated just by observing this one particular sila. And that makes the people so unbalanced, they don't practice samadhi, they don't practice vipashna, they don't practice panya, and they get stuck only with sila because they have stretched it so much. Vata, you take a vow, and you become so attached to this vow, and again you stretch it, stretch it, stretch it to such an extreme, nothing wrong in sila, it's so important. Nothing wrong in vata, taking vow, it is so important, like you take a vow, after midday you won't take any meals, it's a good vow, it helps you in your meditation, or at times you take a vow, you will fast for the whole day, nothing wrong, it keeps you healthy. But then people start stretching it to such an extent, you fasted for one day, I will fast for two days, I am a bigger dhamma person than you are, two days I will fast for five days, five days, I will fast for ten days, twenty days, one month, stretching, stretching, the essence gets lost, the purpose gets lost, one gets so much attached to this sila and to this vata that the other important parts of dhamma like samadhi, like panya is lost to the country. And this was the situation of kuru at that time, people are good in sila, well it is wrong to stretch it to that extent, but still those people who observe sila are definitely much much better than those who know sila, their life is without sila, so these people are much better. Now these people will understand dhamma better because their base is good, although something is wanting and that wanting can be fulfilled by this technique which is being taught now. So this is the place kuru, where the base of morality is there and this is the place where people will understand the details of this technique much better and he gives his technique there. And then when he says, oh bhikkhus come, bhikkhu, what bhikkhu? In the ordinary language of India bhikkhu means a monk, a recluse, but here it doesn't mean that. Not only here in all his teachings when he says bhikkhu, one who is practicing the teaching of dhamma, he may be a layman, he may be a householder, anyone makes no difference, a man, a woman, a monk, a nun, a householder, man, woman, anyone from all these four groups can be a bhikkhu. So he talks, when he calls bhikkhu, he calls bhikkhu to a meditator, oh meditators. And then he says, now here it starts, his discourse. Ekayanu ayam bhikkave maggu, ekayanu, one and only path, ekayanu maggu ayam bhikkave, path maggu, sattanam visuddhiya, to purify the individuals. That means to purify the mind of the individual, mental purification is the real purification, one may keep on washing one's body at the external level, this is not the purification of the individual, the mind should get purified, sattanam visuddhiya. Then what this purification does, soka paridevanam samatikamaya, soka. Great grief, mental grief, very deep grief is soka. Soka paridevanam, and with this mental grief inside, it manifests itself at the physical level, one starts crying, weeping, lamenting, samatikamaya, this path will help the meditator to transcend this, to cross this over. As you practice this technique, no more crying, no more weeping, no more lamentation, and such deep griefs, they come on the surface and pass away, you pass over them. And then, dukkha domanasanam atthangamaya, dukkha domanas, again domanas is the unpleasant feeling of the mind, mind feels unhappy, is domanas. And dukkha, the sensations on the body, unpleasant sensations on the body is dukkha, unpleasant feeling of the mind is domanas atthangamaya, to eradicate that, to finish that, this technique will help. You start from the very gross reality, very gross miseries, and you come to the subtler miseries, subtler miseries, subtler miseries, till you eradicate total miseries, no more misery. When you are too much in mental grief, then you cry and weep, this is so gross, both of them are so gross. Then the misery of mind is still there, some unpleasantness is there in the mind, domanasanam, and there is sensation on the body which is unpleasant, that also goes away by this technique. Nyayas adhigamaya, to help one to walk on the path of truth, nyayas. If you don't walk on the path of truth, if you work with imagination, then the previous thing, whatever I said, cannot be attained. Your misery from the deepest level cannot be taken out, if you just work with some kind of contemplation, some kind of imagination, then your surface of the mind is working to purify itself, surface of the mind gets purified, no doubt by that, but the deepest level of the mind, where you have these deep rooted complexes, they can't come out. They will come out only when you start observing the reality as it is pertaining to mind and matter and the interconnection between the two, and you keep on observing, observing, observing, observing, from the gross apparent truth to deeper, deeper, deeper, till you reach the ultimate truth, the subtlest ultimate truth pertaining to the matter, subtlest ultimate truth pertaining to the mind, pertaining to the mental contents, and thus you are working with the truth, truth that you experience, not the truth experienced by a Buddha. The truth experienced by Buddha can liberate only one person and that person was Buddha only who was liberated. He can only show the path, every, each individual has to walk over the path step by step and must experience the truth oneself directly, directly from the grossest reality to the subtlest, subtlest, subtlest reality. So that is called nyayas adhigamaya, gamaya, you walk on it, adhigamaya, high road, you are walking on the high road of liberation, nibbanas sacchikiriaya, and where it takes your observation of the truth from the grossest apparent reality moving towards subtlest, subtlest, but truth, no imagination, subtlest, subtlest, subtlest, subtlest reality pertaining to the entire mind matter field and then you transcend and witness something which is beyond mind and matter and which is called nibbana. The entire field of mind and matter is the field where things keep on arising, passing, arising, passing, arising, passing, sometimes arising at a very gross level, it arises seem to stay for some time and then passes away, it arises seem to stay for some time and passes away, as you go deeper, deeper, deeper, you notice that it arises, passes, arises, passes with great rapidity, even at the subtlest level there is some oscillation going on, arising, passing, arising, passing is going on, so entire field of mind and matter is the field of arising, passing, arising, passing, this is what one has to experience, not just accept it at the intellectual level, one has to experience it, then a stage comes where you transcend this field of mind and matter, you transcend this field of anicca, arising, passing, arising, passing, and something is experienced, the ultimate truth which is beyond mind and matter, where nothing arises, nothing passes away, but no words can explain it, because this is the experience where all your sense organs stop working. When somebody is in that stage of nibbana, while practicing vipashyana, one comes to the stage where one has transcended the entire field of mind and matter and is now experiencing nibbana, this experience of nibbana is beyond mind and matter, beyond the entire sensorium, all the six sense organs stop working, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind, they stop working, this is the experience beyond the sensual field, sensory field, and coming back from that, this experience may be for a few moments, this experience can be for a few seconds, can be for a few minutes, can be for a few hours, it depends, but when you come back again, in this field, the sensorium field, the field of mind and matter, you are a changed person altogether, but you can't explain what you experienced, how will you explain, you don't have the tools to explain, that experience was experienced beyond the sense organs, and it cannot be explained by these sense organs, and it cannot be understood by the people with the sense organs, it has to be experienced by each individual, the entire path is a path of experience, experience, if you play the game of intellect, then of course you can discuss it, you give a big description of it, because you understood the intellect level, and you try to explain again at the intellect level, and people also try to understand at the intellect level, that doesn't work, the entire path must be experience, experience, that is why the dhamma, the six qualities of dhamma that he gave, the last and the most important quality of dhamma, the dhamma must be experienced by each individual within oneself, directly by oneself, you have to experience it yourself, vedana is experiencing, you experience the truth within yourself, and as you start observing and feeling and experiencing the truth within yourself, from the process, you keep on moving, moving, moving, you explore the entire field of mind and matter, and then you experience something which is beyond mind and matter, so the entire field of observing the truth personally, at the experiential level, now when he says, to people who have not walked on this path deeply, or who have not walked at all, outsiders, they will feel uncomfortable, what this person says, this is the only path, this is very narrow minded outlook, there can be so many paths, why only this path, why he says this is the only path, but those who walk over the path, it becomes so clear, what is path after all, law of nature is universal, law of nature is not different for followers of Budhha, law of nature is not different for those who call themselves Hindus, or those who call themselves Christian, or those who call themselves Muslims, law of nature is law of nature, and he wants us to experience the law of nature, to understand the law of nature, the truth, the law which is applicable to one and all, the dhamma which is applicable to one and all, the nature the characteristic, Like the characteristic of fire is to burn. Anyone who places his hand on the fire is bound to get burned. The fire will not discriminate. Fire will not see that the hand is of the hand of a Hindu or a Buddhist or a Christian or a Australian or a New Zealander or an American. Anyone who puts the hand on the fire is bound to get burned. I don't like burning my hand. So I better keep my hand away from the fire. This is law of nature. This is dhamma. This is what it teaches. This is universal. Because the law is universal, therefore the path has to be universal. It can't be sectarian. And universal path can be only one. Because the law is only one. Buddha or no Buddha, the law is law. It remains. Even when somebody does not become Buddha, the law of nature is there. It remains. Even when somebody becomes a Buddha, the law of nature is there. And even after Buddha, the law of nature is there. Like someone by the name of Newton discovered this law of gravity. Newton or no Newton, this law of gravity was there even before Newton. Even at the time of Newton, even after Newton, it was good that somebody discovered it and placed before it. We make use of it. The law of relativity, somebody by the name of Einstein found it out. It was there. Whether Einstein or no Einstein, even before Einstein, the law of relativity was there at the time of Einstein, and even after Einstein, similarly, dhamma is there. If this, this is there, this result is bound to come, law of nature. If you do not want this result to come, then this, this should be avoided, law of nature. You keep this and this, and you don't want the result, not possible. A kaino maggo in the sense that you follow the law of nature, and law of nature is one and only one. Two parts of hydrogen, one part of oxygen. This results in moisture, in water, law of nature. This is law, this is dhamma. If there is no oxygen, in a planet there is no oxygen, or no hydrogen, there is no water, no moisture, law of nature. This is what you will understand the whole path as you proceed, you have worked already, and you will work much deeper, that if this, this happens, this result is bound to come. And if you don't want this result, because the result is not pleasant to you, it's misery, and you want to come out of misery, then this, this should not happen, you have to remove, you have to remove the cause, and the result is automatically removed. Without removing the cause, somebody feels that I will get liberated from the fruit of this cause, the unpleasant fruit of this cause, the bitter fruit of this cause, because somebody, some supernatural power will be very kind to me, that in spite of all the impurities in my mind, this person will liberate me. Well, this is just wishful thinking, it does not happen. Everyone has to work, and this is the way, the law, the nature, that you have to eradicate your impurities, you have to eradicate your present habit, pattern, full of ignorance, where you keep on generating sankaras, and as a result of which you keep on suffering from misery. This pattern of your habit, at a very deep level of the mind, has to be changed, and this is what is being done. That is why Ekayanu Maggu, Ekayanu Maggu. And what is this Ekayanu Maggu? Kaaye Kayanupassi Viharati, Aatapi Sampajanau Satima, Vinaya Loke Abhijya Dho Manasang. One witnesses the reality of the body within the body, Kaaye Kayanupassi, Aatapi, very ardently, diligently, Sampajanau with wisdom, the wisdom of arising, passing, arising, passing, Satima with awareness. You are directly experiencing the truth about your body within your body. And so also, Vedanasu Vedananupassi Viharati, you are observing the truth of these body sensations within body sensations, you are not imagining them, you are experiencing them, you have a direct experience of that. Vedanasu Vedananupassi Viharati, Aatapi Sampajanau Satima, very diligently, with awareness, with wisdom. Chitte Chittanupassi Viharati, similarly observing the reality of mind within the mind. In the meantime, understand that all the four Satipatthanas, observing the truth pertaining to the body, observing the truth pertaining to the sensations on the body, observing the truth pertaining to the mind, observing the truth pertaining to the contents of the mind, all these four must be experienced by each meditator directly, himself or herself. Just intellectualizing it does not help you. Now again, let me start. Start again with the breath coming in, going out, coming in, going out, deep, shallow, whatever it is, and the sensation on this area. You are aware of this area. And you have come to a very serious course with all the atmosphere around you. So serious. Everybody is working so seriously. No disturbance for the new students. Make use of it. Make use of it, not obliging anybody else, for your own good, for your own benefit, for your own liberation. To enjoy real peace, real harmony, real happiness. segments.text: The second day of the Satipatthana course is over.
This evening let us go through this discourse and understand in relation to the actual practice
that we are doing.
The name of the discourse is Mahasatipatthana Sutthana, Sutthana means discourse.
It is said Mahasatipatthana, the word maha means great, big.
That means there is something smaller than this and yes there is another discourse given
by Buddha on Satipatthana which is smaller than this discourse.
This discourse is maha, bigger because it gives, it deals with some more subjects in
detail therefore it is called Mahasatipatthana.
Sati is awareness, a very important faculty of dhamma as we discussed yesterday.
Sati is one of our indriyas, a faculty which one has to master to develop in dhamma.
Sati is one of the bala, the forces, the strength which one must develop to master dhamma.
Sati is one of the factors of enlightenment which one has to develop to get fully enlightened.
Sati is also one of the eight full noble paths, samma, sati.
Sati plays a very important role in the practice of dhamma.
The literal meaning of the word sati is and very commonly used nowadays in other languages
of India, present languages of India as smriti which means memory, remembrance.
But when you practice vipashyana there is no memory involved, you are not remembering
something of the past.
Here what you have to remember is, remember your object of meditation.
That means the reality within the framework of the body, the reality pertaining to mind
and matter.
You should always remember that your mind does not wander away from this reality.
That is in that sense you can say remembrance.
But in a better way of understanding let us say sati means awareness and this is what
it is.
You are aware.
You can't be aware of the past, you can't be aware of the future.
You can be aware of the present.
The reality of this moment as it is, this is sati, pathana.
One gets established.
The word pa says extensively, you get established extensively.
What extensively?
That means it is not mere awareness, along with that awareness there is element of panya,
element of wisdom.
You are not merely aware of the truth pertaining to mind and matter, you are also aware of
the nature of this truth pertaining to mind and matter, how it keeps on arising, passing
away, arising, passing away, how it is a source of misery, how it is no I, no mind, how it
is substance-less.
All that has not to be understood merely at the intellectual level with direct experience.
And therefore pathana, panya, the bhavanamaya panya is there, with your own direct experience
you develop your awareness with the wisdom which makes you understand the reality in
its true nature, not just as it appears to be, not just as it seems to be, but in its
true nature and that is why it is maha sati pathana sutta.
When the discourse starts, evam me sutam, this is what was heard by me, this was heard
by me.
These are not the words of buddha, somebody else says, this was heard by me.
These are the words of someone else, there is a history behind it and a very important
history which a vipassana meditator should know.
At the ripened age of 80 years when buddha passed away, most of his students who were
present at that time and who had reached the final goal of arhanthood, fully liberated,
they understood the law of nature, everyone who takes birth has to pass away.
Whether one is buddha or an ordinary person makes no difference.
When time ripens, one has to pass away.
For those who were not developed in dhamma, they felt very sorry, very sad, some of them
even started crying.
There was one person who felt very happy.
An old monk, in age old, not in wisdom, he felt very happy, oh good, this old man has
passed away.
All the time we were under his clutches, do this, don't do this, do this, don't do this,
now we are free to do whatever we like.
One of his teachings, attahi attanonathu, you are your own master, now I can be my own
master, wonderful.
That shows that such elements had entered in the sangha who were not interested in dhamma.
They just took robes because they found by entering the sangha, becoming a monk in the
name of buddha, will give them some status in the society.
They can live a comfortable life, people will give more arms to them than they would have
received otherwise, and they will get more respect, they were not interested in dhamma.
Now this person, I feel extremely grateful to this person, thankful to this person, why?
Because when he announced that wonderful buddha has passed away, one of the chief disciples
of buddha, when he heard this, he thought even today if there are such people, what
is going to happen in the future, later on such elements will become predominant, and
they will just distort the teaching of buddha in their own way, and actually this happened
also after some time.
How to save it?
The words of buddha, the teachings of buddha, he became enlightened at the age of 35, and
he passed away at the age of 80, for 45 years, day and night, hardly two or three hours he
will lie down for sleep, which is not sleep, awareness and equanimity, awareness and wisdom,
to give rest to the body, rest of the time he was just teaching dhamma.
He taught, he gave 82,000 sermons.
Over 2,000 sermons were given by leading disciples of buddha, who were urhans.
So in all 84,000 sermons.
Now this elderly disciple, by the name of Mahakassapa, he decides that all the teaching
of buddha must be compiled together, and we should try to preserve it for the coming
generations, so that people do not change it.
Quite possible later on, persons like this fellow will put their own words in the mouth
of buddha and they will say, buddha said so, they will take freedom from certain disciplines
which are very essential for the progress of dhamma, and they will say, buddha gave
this permission, and things like that, which after a few centuries it did happen.
We must preserve the actual words of buddha, while there are people who are direct disciples
of buddha, who are eyewitness to buddha's teaching, who heard buddha's teaching.
So he decided to call a meeting of 500 urhans, fully liberated persons, elderly persons,
elderly monks, let us sit together and recite all the teachings of buddha, compile them,
and announce it as authenticated.
This is just immediately after the death of buddha.
If this is compiled after 100 years or 200 years, people may accept, may not accept,
it should be done now.
So this Mahakasapa, a very wise person, he made this decision, he gathered 500 elderly
urhans, well even a few handful could do that, but just to impress the people of that time
and people of future, 500 of them joined together, and they read out every word, they recited
every word of buddha, and then gave it a seal of authenticity.
When he selected 500, somebody said no, this congregation, this gathering will not be
a perfect gathering unless we have ananda as one of the members.
So have only 499, let ananda be a member to make it 500.
Now who is this ananda?
Buddha was cousin brother of buddha, Gautama the buddha, was born on the same day as Gautama
the buddha was born.
He was with him in the childhood, he was with him during the youth, and when buddha renounced
the householder's life, went out and became enlightened, then he was one amongst many
family members who also renounced their householder's life and joined him, and since then he was
with him all the time.
When buddha started teaching, the number of followers started spreading, the work started
spreading, naturally he wanted some assistant, a number of assistants came near him to help
him, to serve him, but quite a few of them came with some motives, the motive was, here
he is a fully enlightened person, he is against these miracles, he has the power of miracles,
no doubt, but he doesn't want his followers to show miracles.
If I am very close to him, I will be fortunate to see some of the miracles being performed
by him, such motive was there with some of these attendants, personal attendants.
Buddha had refused to answer certain questions, philosophical questions, he said they are
useless, meaningless, don't waste your time on them.
Now some attendants thought that he doesn't want to say anything on this subject in public,
but perhaps if I am very close, then he may explain, I better be very close, I better
serve.
Such people could not stay with him longer, sooner or later they have to leave.
People keep on changing and as he grew in age, he became 55 years old, getting old,
so people thought that there must be a stable personal assistant with him, he also accepted
yes some responsible stable personal assistant, a private secretary is necessary.
Many of the elderly monks were very eager to take that post, to serve him so closely,
but Buddha had a liking towards Ananda, and Ananda is mum, he doesn't say a word, people
know that if Ananda says yes, Buddha will accept him, Ananda does not say yes, when
they persuaded him he said I have got my terms, if Buddha accepts my terms, then I will be
his personal assistant, somebody putting terms before Buddha to be a personal assistant,
what are your terms?
He put up some seven or eight terms, and out of that one was very healthy terms, very wholesome
terms.
One of that was that whenever you give any discourse anywhere, if I am present, perfectly
alright, if by any reason I am not present and you give a discourse, then when you come
back you must repeat that discourse to me.
Buddha accepted all his conditions, including this, so from the age of 55 to the age of
80, 25 years, every discourse that Buddha gave was heard by this person, Ananda, even
the discourses before that also were heard by him, but these 25 years he was like a shadow
with Buddha, every discourse was heard by him, and here was a wonderful person, he had
such a wonderful faculty, from some of his good parmes of the past, and also due to
his practice of this life, he had developed the faculty of memory, he hears something
once, enough, it is like tape recorded, what you are doing here, it is like computerized,
anytime you ask anything, he will just repeat word to word, this was his wonderful faculty.
So people said if Ananda is not there, something is missing, he should be there, but he can't
be there, because this is a gathering of Arhans, and he is not an Arhan.
Understand Ananda served Buddha for 25 years, so close to him, Ananda was his cousin brother,
so close to him, Ananda was his great devotee, so close to him, and yet he could not become
Arhan, he was only Sotapanna, the first stage of liberation, when one experiences the liberation
stage, the stage beyond mind and matter for the first time, very important stage, but
still it is the first stage of liberation, after that you have got higher stage, you
have got higher stage than that, and then you have the highest stage of Arhan, and here
he is having reached only the first stage, this again for us to understand that Buddha
cannot liberate anybody, each individual has to work out one's own salvation, he had no
time, he was just serving Buddha all the time, he could not progress, although he knew
Dhamma perfectly well, not one, not two, thousands of persons whom he taught became Arhans, and
he himself was not Arhan, and in this gathering, how can a known Arhan be there, so Mahakasrapa
goes to him and tells him, well look, well look, Vandivalananda, you were very busy
serving Buddha, now Buddha is no more, you know the technique so well, because your own

become Arhan, so that you can come in our gathering, join our gathering, this is the
aim that we have of this gathering, and you will be very great asset to it, Ananda was
very glad, wonderful, yes, I didn't have much time before, now I have got time, nothing
else, all time is there at my disposal, wait for few days, I will practice, I will become
Arhanth and join you, and he started working, started working very vigorously, I must become
an Arhanth, I must become an Arhanth, when he was teaching others, he used to say, don't
develop ego, this ego is dangerous for you, it will be an obstacle, and when he practices
himself, this ego becomes important, I must become Arhanth, I must become Arhanth, many
a time the teacher forgets what he teaches others, when he practices himself, he forgets
his own teaching and this is what happened, he didn't move an inch, now tomorrow they
have to start this conference, and Mahakasrappa comes to Ananda and tells him, look we have
waited so long, we can't be waiting, there are 499 persons waiting for the conference
to start by tomorrow morning, you are Arhanth or no Arhanth, if you are no Arhanth, I take
somebody else, I will start my work, if you are Arhanth, you are welcome, yes, yes, yes,
one night more, I will try this one night more, and again try, try, I must become Arhanth,
this is the only night for me, I must become Arhanth, the first part of the night, the
middle part of the night, the last part of the night, light passes away, the sun is rising,
he is so exhausted, he doesn't cry, at least this good quality, he is not successful, and
that much he knows that one should not cry when one is not successful, he accept the
fact, well I accept the fact, I am not an Arhanth, now let me take rest, let me take

moment as it is, when he was aiming for something to become Arhanth, his mind was always in
the future, not in the present, and now I am not an Arhanth, he accept this reality,
I am just a Sotapanna, I am taking rest, I am taking rest, and observing the sensations

what did Buddha say? All the teachings of Buddha were compiled, and three divisions
were made, that is why they are called Ti Pitika, Ti means three, Pitika means baskets,

fully explained how they interact, how one starts influencing the other, how the matter
